theme: TripAdvisor datasets: hotel/vacation-rental reviews, review velocity, TripAdvisor rentals, scraper repos
queries_run: site:github.com tripadvisor reviews dataset csv (WebSearch tool exhausted session-wide before returning; treated as failed)
tripadvisor scraper github hotel reviews (WebSearch exhausted)
tripadvisor vacation rental dataset github (WebSearch exhausted)
bing.com/search site:github.com tripadvisor reviews dataset (no github results surfaced)
marginalia-search.com github tripadvisor rentals dataset vacation (no results)
libraries.io search tripadvisor (login wall, no results)
paperswithcode.com/dataset/hotelrec and search=tripadvisor (dead, redirects to huggingface trending)
direct WebFetch verification of ~15 individual candidate repo URLs

candidates.name: HotelRec
candidates.what_it_holds: ~50 million TripAdvisor hotel reviews (largest public hotel-review dataset per the authors, vs 0.9M in prior academic sets). Each review has hotel URL, reviewer username, date, overall rating, title, text, and sub-ratings (sleep quality, value, rooms, service, cleanliness, location). International coverage (sample shows Italian hotels; likely global given TripAdvisor's footprint). Actual data is not committed to the repo -- hosted on a SWITCHdrive link, restricted to academic research use only. Cites Antognini & Faltings, LREC 2020. Repo itself: 17 commits, README + download pointer.
candidates.why_useful: By far the largest and longest-running TripAdvisor review corpus found. A review-velocity / sub-rating time series built from this (filtered to years with real dates, cross-referenced to ABNB peer-set cities) could proxy hotel demand momentum and sentiment ahead of MAR/HLT RevPAR releases -- addresses gap #8 (hotel supply/demand) indirectly via review flow as a leading indicator, and gap #20 partially (party-size/length-of-stay not present but trip-type sub-ratings sometimes are). Academic-only license limits direct commercial reuse but fine for an internal model.
candidates.license: Academic research only (non-commercial); no open-source license stated for the download itself
candidates.time_coverage: Reviews with dates as early as ~2010 in samples shown; full range not confirmed

candidates.name: argilla/tripadvisor-hotel-reviews
candidates.what_it_holds: 20,500 TripAdvisor hotel reviews (the well-known 'TripAdvisor Hotel Reviews' Kaggle set, mirrored/curated on Hugging Face by Argilla with added sentiment labels 1-5, confidence scores, text length). Reviews span international hotels (Florence, Barcelona, Hawaii, Amsterdam, Paris, Singapore, Punta Cana, Berlin, Tokyo, etc.), dates roughly 2004-2008 in visible samples. Parquet format, loadable via HF `datasets` or pandas.
candidates.why_useful: Small but clean, ready-to-load, dated review sample across many geographies; could serve as a spot-check / calibration set for any review-velocity or sentiment method before scaling to HotelRec. Marginal versus HotelRec for size but easier to pull (no gated download).
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Overlaps conceptually with Booking.com 515k-review Kaggle set already held, but TripAdvisor source is new

candidates.name: factden/tripadvisor-hotel-reviews-api
candidates.what_it_holds: Apify-actor source code (MIT licensed) that pulls per-review data from TripAdvisor hotels/restaurants/attractions/airlines: rating, title, full text, language + machine-translation flag, reviewer profile, owner responses, sub-ratings (rooms, cleanliness, etc.), plus property records (rankings, amenities, address, TripAdvisor AI-generated review summaries). Repo commits real committed sample output: reviews.sample.json, places.sample.json, and a CSV from a live 'W Barcelona' run. Usage-based paid pricing (~$0.45/1,000 reviews, ~$2.00/1,000 property records) beyond a free monthly credit tier; global city/country filtering via 'Discover' mode. Does NOT cover TripAdvisor vacation rentals, only hotels/restaurants/attractions.
candidates.why_useful: A maintained, documented, MIT-licensed method to pull fresh TripAdvisor hotel review counts and text at low marginal cost, city-filterable -- usable as a review-velocity nowcast input for competitor hotel demand (parallel to the ABNB reviews-based stays index already built over 123 Inside Airbnb markets). Has real committed sample data to inspect the schema without paying.
candidates.license: MIT (code); Apify platform usage is metered/paid beyond free tier
candidates.time_coverage: Live/current pulls only, not historical archive
candidates.size_hint: sample files only (few KB); production pulls scale to any size at cost
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: None (new method for hotel review velocity)

candidates.name: omkarcloud/tripadvisor-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: 212-star MIT-licensed scraper/API wrapper extracting hotel, restaurant, attraction and cruise data from TripAdvisor: names, ratings, review counts, pricing, coordinates, amenities, award badges, rankings. JSON via REST endpoints; also crawls property websites for emails/phones/social/tech stack. 45+ locales, 145+ currencies. Free tier 200 requests/month. No dataset files committed, only JSON response examples in docs.
candidates.why_useful: Highest-starred, actively maintained general-purpose TripAdvisor extraction tool; could be pointed at hotel markets that overlap the Inside Airbnb 13/34/120-market panels to build a competing-supply review/price signal. Method only, no data.

candidates.name: magic890/tripadvisor-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: 80-star Scrapy-based scraper targeting TripAdvisor restaurant listings (command shown: `scrapy crawl tripadvisor-restaurant`). Outputs JSON-lines by default. No sample data committed. GPL-3.0 licensed; educational-use disclaimer in README about possible ToS conflicts.
candidates.why_useful: Restaurant demand/velocity is a weak but free proxy for local tourism activity (adjacent to OpenTable seated-diner data already held); low direct relevance to ABNB but easy to adapt.

candidates.name: maxCopell/tripadvisor-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: 50-star Apify-actor source ('source actor for other tripadvisor actors') extracting TripAdvisor restaurants, hotels and places; example.json + INPUT_SCHEMA.json only, no bulk data committed; Dockerized. 118 commits, 17 open issues.
candidates.why_useful: Feeds several downstream TripAdvisor actors on Apify; same general-purpose value as omkarcloud's scraper, redundant with it for our purposes.

candidates.name: andorfermichael/tripadvisor-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: 36-star archived (read-only since ~Apr 2023) scraper that pulls hotel reviews across an entire city on TripAdvisor (examples: NYC, Paris, Vienna) into timestamped directories plus a 'totalizer' script to consolidate all reviews/hotel info into one output. Uses pickle-based caching keyed to a TripAdvisor location ID.
candidates.why_useful: City-level bulk hotel-review pull is closer to what a 'review velocity by market' construction needs than single-property scrapers; archived/unmaintained so TripAdvisor's current page structure will likely have broken it, but the approach and location-ID list are reusable.
candidates.geography: any city with a TripAdvisor location ID; examples NYC, Paris, Vienna
candidates.size_hint: no data committed (code produces `data/`, `pickle/`, `totalized/` output dirs)

candidates.name: jios325/tripadvisor-reviews-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Small (2-star, 1-commit) MIT-licensed scraper using TripAdvisor's GraphQL API directly (via curl_cffi TLS fingerprinting, no Selenium/Playwright needed) to pull 21 structured review fields (ratings, text, dates, reviewer info, management responses) per hotel. Outputs JSON, CSV, or SQL INSERT statements. No committed sample data; ships proxies.txt.example.
candidates.why_useful: Lightweight, dependency-free, up-to-date (GraphQL, not scraping rendered HTML) method -- likely to survive longer against TripAdvisor's anti-bot changes than Selenium-based scrapers above. Method only.

candidates.name: factden/booking-com-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Apify-actor source (part of the same factden org as the TripAdvisor scraper above) extracting Booking.com hotel information, live per-room pricing, availability calendars, and guest reviews.
candidates.why_useful: Directly extends the Booking.com data already held (515k Kaggle reviews, RecTour24) with a live pricing/availability puller -- closest thing found to a free realised-ADR/occupancy proxy for gap #2, if run against a fixed hotel panel over time to build a price time series.
candidates.license: MIT (consistent with sibling repos; not independently confirmed)
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Adjacent to existing Booking.com Kaggle/RecTour24 holdings but adds live pricing capability they lack

candidates.name: factden/expedia-hotel-reviews-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Apify-actor source scraping all 7 Expedia Group brands (Expedia, Hotels.com, Orbitz, Travelocity, Vrbo, etc. under one group) for guest ratings, category sub-ratings, review text, and owner responses.
candidates.why_useful: Covers Vrbo indirectly as an Expedia-Group brand -- one of the named competitor gaps (#9). No committed data seen; method only.
candidates.license: not independently confirmed (org sibling repos are MIT)

candidates.name: factden/ctrip-trip-reviews-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Apify-actor extracting Trip.com and Ctrip (携程) hotel reviews, both international and Chinese-language, with sub-ratings, owner responses, and reviewer geography.
candidates.why_useful: One of the only leads found on this whole sweep touching Chinese OTA data (gap #9 names Tujia/Xiaozhu specifically; Ctrip/Trip.com is the dominant Chinese OTA and a reasonable proxy for Chinese outbound travel demand, relevant to ABNB's APAC push).

candidates.name: factden/reports
candidates.what_it_holds: Repo advertised as providing free sample datasets from FactDen's scrapers, but the only file actually present is `saas-battlecard-atlas-2026-sample.csv` (a sample from 50,000 G2.com software reviews, 30+ columns) -- no TripAdvisor, Airbnb, Booking, or Hotels.com sample data despite the org maintaining scrapers for all of them.
candidates.why_useful: Checked because it looked promising (a committed sample-data repo from an org with 20+ scrapers) but turned out irrelevant to travel/lodging. Flagging so nobody re-checks it expecting travel data.
candidates.license: stated 'public G2 review data provided for evaluation purposes'

candidates.name: MichiganNLP/multilingual_reviews_deception
candidates.what_it_holds: NAACL 2025 Findings paper repo, 'Multilingual Deception Detection of GPT-generated Hotel Reviews'. Committed `all_data.csv` labels real vs. GPT-4-generated hotel reviews (label 0 = real, 1 = fake/LLM-generated); generation code in LLM_generation.py; XLM-RoBERTa multilingual modeling. Source platform of the 'real' reviews not confirmed as TripAdvisor specifically in the fetched content. MIT licensed.
candidates.why_useful: Marginal for KPI forecasting, but relevant to a review-authenticity/fake-review-detection angle if the team ever wants to sanity-check whether a review-velocity signal (ours or a competitor's) is contaminated by synthetic reviews. Low priority for now.

candidates.name: rgmining/tripadvisor
candidates.what_it_holds: Python loader (GPLv3, 86 commits, archived Oct 22 2025 / read-only) for a TripAdvisor reviews dataset (~1.17M reviewers) originally hosted by Tsinghua University's COAI lab for 'Latent Aspect Rating Analysis' research (Wang, Lu & Zhai, KDD 2010/2011). README explicitly states the underlying dataset 'is no longer accessible.'
candidates.why_useful: Dead end -- flagging only so it is not re-investigated. The dataset host is gone and the repo is archived.

notes: Both the WebSearch tool and github.com's own search/topic pages hit rate limits partway through this run (WebSearch: 'session has used its web search budget 200 of 200' -- this is a SHARED cross-agent budget in this sweep, likely exhausted by earlier scouts before I ran any query; github.com/search: HTTP 429 with Retry-After 3600 on repeated attempts). Standard search engines (Bing via WebFetch, DuckDuckGo html/lite) returned no usable github.com links -- DuckDuckGo served a CAPTCHA wall on both html.duckduckgo.com and lite.duckduckgo.com. Kaggle and libraries.io pages are JS-rendered and returned no content via WebFetch. paperswithcode.com appears to be dead/redirecting generically to huggingface.co/papers/trending regardless of query. Marginalia Search worked partially but returned mostly non-GitHub blog/PDF hits for TripAdvisor queries and nothing for the 'rentals/vacation' query. The workaround that actually produced results was fetching GitHub's static /topics/<topic> pages directly (topics: tripadvisor, tripadvisor-scraper, hotel-reviews) plus following up on named organizations/users found there (factden, in particular, had 22 repos once its user page was fetched directly after the org page 404'd). Recommend future scouts on this sweep try GitHub topic pages and named-org user pages as a 429-resistant fallback when github.com/search itself is rate-limited. Did NOT find: (a) any repo specifically scraping 'TripAdvisor Rentals' (the vacation-rental line TripAdvisor discontinued/folded from FlipKey) -- the flipkey query could not run (429) and no topic/organic result surfaced one; a follow-up scout with a working github.com/search should try 'flipkey', 'tripadvisor rentals', 'tripadvisor vacation rental'; (b) any point-in-time/vintage TripAdvisor review archive (e.g., Wayback-scraped historical review counts) -- everything found is either a live-pull scraper or a single-vintage academic dump, nothing addresses gap #4's need for point-in-time review-count history; (c) any TripAdvisor 'Travelers' Choice' award history dataset, which would be a clean annual quality-ranking panel if it exists. All of these are worth a dedicated follow-up once github.com/search rate limits clear.
